claims.statement: startNextSession and startPlannedSession resume the most recently performed unfinished session of the active program when it has a program_day_id, otherwise insert a workout_session stamped with the derived program_day_id, week_index, and cookie exercise swaps, then delete the plan cookie only after the insert succeeds.

Session day and week are derived from the count of finished sessions for the active program, not a stored cursor: week is floor(completed / days.length) + 1 and the day is days[completed % days.length]. The session page later reads the persisted week_index and program_day_id rather than recounting.
A planned start whose planKey no longer matches the derived next workout redirects to /workout/next instead of inserting a session from a stale plan.

SessionPage hydrates slot exercise identity as the explicit exercise_swaps entry when present, otherwise the most recently logged exercise for that program_slot_id, otherwise the folded Fluid prescription, so an in-session swap survives reload before the first set is logged. Sets are grouped by slot, not exercise.

SessionPage does not await record history. It streams recordsPromise and catches a load failure as null so a PR-history failure or the first-set history page does not suspend the session page or remount the layout-scoped rest timer.

Every session server action gates on getClaims and redirects to /login when claims.sub is missing. logSet and finishSession additionally require an owner-scoped session row, while deleteSet selects and deletes by set id and relies on RLS for ownership.

logSet rejects unresolved station templates, invalid weight/reps, and missing RIR before insert. It does not require the session to be unfinished. set_index is a count scoped to (session, program_slot_id) or, for ad-hoc sets, (session, exercise_id).

A new set is marked is_calibration only when the exercise needsCalibration and this is the first exact-id set ever. A later set of that variant is not a calibration set, barbell-station variants are not calibrated, and leftover template rows on a different exercise_id are not rewritten.

logSet is idempotent per (session_id, idempotency_key) via a partial unique index. On Postgres 23505 with a supplied key it re-reads and returns the existing row with recomputeWarning null and does not recompute stats. The client generates one UUID per log intent and reuses it across retryServerAction attempts.

If recomputeAndUpsertStat throws after a successful log, edit, or delete, the set mutation still succeeds and returns a recomputeWarning. SlotCard shows that warning with a Retry stats update action that calls retryRecomputeStat and does not insert another set. This warning is distinct from a failed set write, which reverts the optimistic row and shows a danger error.

The rest timer is one layout-scoped instance per session. It stores an absolute end timestamp in memory and sessionStorage, recomputes remaining from that timestamp every 250ms, treats an expired stored timestamp as absent, and is rendered by both the session loading and error fallbacks so a logged-set refresh does not clear it.

Rest starts optimistically when a set is logged, before the server write resolves, using the slot rest_seconds or the profile default. A failed write does not roll the timer back. Finishing or viewing a finished session disables the provider, clears the stored end timestamp, and cancels the scheduled notification.

Rest completion vibrates unconditionally, plays Web Audio beeps only when profile.rest_tone_enabled is on, and shows a system notification only when Notification permission is granted. Permission is requested at rest start. The rest service worker schedules that same end timestamp and does not cache documents or add offline sync.

Readiness is a 1-5 integer that the UI prompts only before any hydrated set exists on an unfinished session. saveSessionReadiness rejects a finished session and any session that already has a set_log row, so readiness cannot be retconned after training starts.

Joint pain and the session note are optional fields on workout_session. finishSession can persist them in the finish call. Later edits go through updateSessionFeedback, which writes joint_pain and notes only and does not change finished_at.

finishSession loads the record replay before writing finished_at. A failed history read or finish update leaves finished_at null and does not return a success summary. The finished_at update is guarded by is(finished_at, null), so reopening the summary does not move the original finish time.

After a successful finish, the client skips rest and router.replace navigates to the recap route. The recap page redirects to the live session when finished_at is null and notFound when the session row is missing. The recap route loads records itself and does not render the finish action's topE1rm payload.
Editing or deleting sets after finish is allowed and recalculates the recap through the same replay, but does not change finished_at. A failed edit or delete preserves the previously valid records.

workoutRecords is a pure replay of persisted sets. It emits rep, e1RM, and top-weight records only when a current eligible set beats a prior baseline at display precision. A first observation is not a record; a later within-workout improvement can be, with a null improvement so no historical delta is invented. Machine templates, warmups, and invalid sets are ineligible.

loadWorkoutRecords pages current sets and prior finished history in 500-row chunks ordered by created_at then id, scoped to exercises touched in the current session. It throws on a read failure instead of inventing a baseline, and does not query history for an empty workout. Live pills, finish, and the recap all consume this loader.

Live achievement pills are slot-filtered from the streamed replay via recordsForSlot and never include optimistic rows. The recap headline uses a single N PRs count only when every record is the same kind; mixed kinds stay a joined string.

recomputeAndUpsertStat rebuilds user_exercise_stat.current_e1rm as the max working-set e1RM for one exact exercise_id. For needsCalibration exercises it anchors personal_coefficient on the first working session, re-anchors while only one session exists, then holds the coefficient. Deleting every working set clears the coefficient and sets coeff_confidence_n to 0.

editSet preserves the bodyweight implied by a bodyweight set's originally persisted e1RM. If that historical bodyweight cannot be recovered, the edited e1RM stays null instead of substituting today's weigh-in.
